s1.where: A page asking me to turn on notifications for the app.
s1.expectation: I am on a page that asks me to turn on notifications from Messenger, probably when the app has just started.
s1.cue: The large heading 'Turn on notifications from Messenger'.

first_pass.why: The heading says plainly what this page is for, and there is little else competing with it.

s2.where: The main page with the list of my chats.
s2.expectation: I am on the main Chats page of Messenger.
s2.cue: The blue 'Chats' word and icon in the bottom row. The top only says 'messenger'.

first_pass.why: The only words in the top strip are the app's own name, 'messenger', which tells me which app I am in, not which part of it. The one thing that places me is the small blue 'Chats' word in the bottom row, and I have to find it underneath a very busy page of round photos, names, a blue banner and 'Add friend' buttons. I get there, but only after scanning the whole screen, and that costs me.
first_pass.solution: Put the name of the place, 'Chats', as a large heading at the top where 'messenger' is now, so I do not have to hunt for the small blue tab at the bottom.

test_cases.task: On the first screen scroll the list down two screens, pause, name the place without scrolling back; then tap the middle and right items of the bottom row and come back with the left one.
test_cases.real_if: You have to hunt or guess to name the place after the pause.
test_cases.not_real_if: You can name it at once from what is on screen.
test_cases.what_happened: I scrolled the chat list down two screens and paused. When I looked back, the top still said only 'messenger' and the whole list was strangers with blue 'Add friend' buttons; not one of my conversations was in view. The only thing that told me I was on Chats was the small blue word at the bottom left, and I had to search for it. When I tapped the middle and right tabs, the top changed to a large 'People' and a large 'Notifications', and only that tab was coloured. That makes the Chats page the odd one out: it is the one page whose name is not at the top. The left tab brought me back to 'messenger'. This is the 'real' result: I had to hunt to name the place.

s2.closing_comment: Every other main page puts its name at the top; only Chats does not, and that is the page I land on most.

s3.where: A side menu with my account name at the top.
s3.expectation: I think I am in a menu panel that has slid out over the main page.
s3.cue: The list of items ('Communities', 'Message requests', 'Archive') and the name 'Ally Cooper' at the top.

first_pass.why: The only large words at the top are a person's name, 'Ally Cooper', with a small arrow. A name tells me whose account it is, not where I am. I can work out from the list ('Communities', 'Message requests', 'Archive', 'Friend requests') that this is a menu that has slid over the main page, but nothing says 'Menu', and with the old page still showing at the right edge I am not sure whether I have left the page or not.
first_pass.solution: A plain heading such as 'Menu' at the top of the panel, with the account name underneath it as a smaller line, and a clear Close button.

test_cases.task: Open the side panel from the first screen, read it, close with Back; open it again from the middle tab and compare; close with Back.
test_cases.real_if: The panel never names itself and never marks where you came from.
test_cases.not_real_if: Something on it tells you what it is and where you are.
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the panel from Chats. At the top was 'Ally Cooper' with a small arrow and a gear, then the list. I closed it with Back. Then I went to People and opened the panel again. It was exactly the same panel, word for word: nothing said 'Menu', and nothing marked that I had come from People rather than Chats. Only a thin grey strip of the page behind showed at the right edge. This is the 'real' result.

s3.closing_comment: A panel that never says 'Menu' and looks the same wherever I open it from leaves me guessing what I have left behind.
